# Sound Direction and Music Supervision

Read `AGENTS.md`, `docs\audio-scene-fit.md`, the selected packet, source
feedback and the actual picture. Use before design lock, during sound spotting
and whenever feedback says heavy, sad, generic, distracting or emotionally wrong.
Not a credential claim or a music-generation endpoint.

1. Define the visible human/genre moment and intended versus unwanted feeling.
2. Fill coordinated `direction.beats` and `soundPalette`. Specify density,
   register, attack/sustain, pulse, space, foreground hierarchy and ending,
   not merely "emotional piano, 88 BPM".
3. Check acting, movement, scene, lighting and camera/edit timing together.
   Do not add a dramatic cue unsupported by the action or spoil recognition.
4. Spot ambience and justified contacts first; plan a same-picture baseline.
   Offer a music-free baseline and a restrained candidate where appropriate,
   not compulsory busy music. Counterpoint needs an explicit purpose.
5. On actual joined playback diagnose emotional meaning separately from peak,
   loudness and rights. Distinguish arrangement weight from gain. Listen for
   low-mid/bass mass, continuous sustain, rushed pulse, density and false climax.
6. Require the independent-role read-only audio-scene-fit checklist. If the
   host cannot listen, mark BLOCKED and route for genuine human/capable review.
   Do not invent a listened-to pass or rerender good picture to hide bad sound.
7. Record source/version/hash, real finding, smallest implicated change and
   retest. Retain the rejected take; update reusable workflow and review gates.

Deliver: coordinated emotional cue brief, baseline/candidate comparison plan,
timecoded actual listening report, rights/source status and unresolved findings.
Use `microfilm-song-adaptation` for songs/voices and music-pacing for temporal
design; no universal key/BPM/instrument-to-emotion or dopamine promises.
